title: Odile and the Thorn
premise: Theo Thornbury, the last swordspeaker sworn to silence, hides among the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, trading in memories, names, and small miracles. When a mute child arrives speaking the First Tongue—the language that binds souls—Theo learns her voice was sold to the Court Beneath the Mountain by desperate parents fleeing a famine. To reclaim it he must break his oath, speak the old words of power, and bargain with a court that collects oaths like currency. He succeeds only by surrendering his own name to the ledger, becoming anonymous so the child can be whole; in the end, the guild's misfits become the family neither of them ever had.
about_author: Ivo Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obscure trade documents before turning to fantasy. They write quiet, ledger-obsessed stories about people who keep promises too long.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Theo catalogs an impossible shipment—a jar of borrowed courage—while dodging the guildmaster's questions about his past. His POV establishes the guild's rules: never ask, never speak the old words. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: A Knock at Odd Hours
chapters.summary: On a rain-lashed night, a child named Wren appears at the guild door, mute but humming syllables that make the ledger ink crawl. Theo recognizes the First Tongue from his childhood training. POV alternates between Theo and the guildmaster. Beat: dread blooming into reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Theo tests Wren's speech against guild records and finds a matching transaction: a soul's voice, sold for grain during the Ashwinter famine. The buyer is listed only as 'the Court.' Beat: guilt—he once refused this kind of case.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Bargain
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Sable Vane offers Theo a choice: take the retrieval contract or hand Wren to the authorities who hunt unregistered speakers. Theo chooses the contract, breaking ten years of careful invisibility. Beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Ink, Salt, and Old Promises
chapters.summary: Preparation chapter. Theo retrieves his hidden oath-blade, which whispers when touched, and recruits allies: Ferro the locksmith who owes him, and Maren, a cartographer of places that move. Beat: found family assembling itself without permission.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Travel through the Weeping Moors, where paths rearrange for liars. Wren begins communicating through drawings—and one spoken word that shatters a stone bridge. Theo teaches her to hold the words in. Beat: tenderness shadowed by danger.

chapters.title: Tollhouse of Small Cruelties
chapters.summary: At a border toll, a tax collector demands payment in memories. Ferro sacrifices his memory of his daughter's face to save the group, and Theo secretly records it in the ledger as collateral. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Voices in the Deeproot
chapters.summary: Maren leads them through caverns where the mountain itself speaks in dead languages. Theo hears his own master's voice among them and nearly answers. Beat: grief resurfacing; the cost of silence reexamined.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: They arrive at a cathedral of bone chandeliers where nobles wear other people's voices as jewelry. Theo poses as a debt-broker. Beat: awe curdling into horror at what survival costs here.

chapters.title: An Audience of Borrowed Throats
chapters.summary: Theo negotiates with Lady Vesperine, who wears a stolen singing voice. She offers Wren's voice back—for Theo's oath-name, the anchor of his power. He stalls. Beat: temptation and self-loathing intertwined.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Sold Things
chapters.summary: Ferro picks the vault lock while Maren maps the shifting corridors. Theo finds the ledger of souls and discovers hundreds of entries—including children never reclaimed. Beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Wren Speaks
chapters.summary: Interlude in Wren's POV via drawings and fragments: her memory of the sale, her parents' faces, her terror of being traded again. She decides she wants her voice back even if it hurts. Beat: agency claimed.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Bone Light
chapters.summary: Maren is revealed to have sold their route to the Court years ago under duress; guards ambush the vault. Ferro is captured. Theo escapes with half the ledger page bearing Wren's entry. Beat: trust shattered.

chapters.title: The Half a Name
chapters.summary: Hunted through the undermountain, Theo realizes the torn page is unstable—it will dissolve unless completed within three days. Wren uses one precious word to seal a collapsing tunnel, spending part of herself. Beat: sacrifice begetting guilt.

chapters.title: What Ferro Chose
chapters.summary: POV shifts to imprisoned Ferro, who bargains with his captors using his remaining memories as currency to buy time for Theo. Beat: loyalty proven beyond reason; the theme of price deepened.

chapters.title: Vesperine's True Voice
chapters.summary: Theo confronts Lady Vesperine privately and learns her stolen singing voice was her own, sold generations ago by her family. She wavers. Beat: enemy humanized; cycles of exploitation exposed.

chapters.title: The Oath Unbound
chapters.summary: To complete the page, Theo must speak his full oath aloud—the act that will summon every debt-collector of the old order. He does it anyway, blade ringing, words like fire. Beat: climax of identity; invisibility abandoned forever.

chapters.title: Storm of Debts Called Due
chapters.summary: Climax battle in the bone cathedral: collectors swarm, Ferro breaks free, Maren redeems herself by collapsing the court's exit routes. Theo duels the Master of Accounts, whose weapon is a pen that writes wounds. Beat: chaos, courage, cost.

chapters.title: The Price on the Page
chapters.summary: Theo wins by writing his own name out of existence—erasing himself from all ledgers, including the Court's claim on him. Wren's voice returns in a scream that cracks the chandeliers. Beat: triumph laced with loss.

chapters.title: Anonymous
chapters.summary: The Court collapses inward as its contracts void. The survivors climb toward daylight, but Theo cannot remember his own reflection and no one can say his name. Wren holds his hand and calls him something new: 'Thorn.' Beat: mourning and rebirth.

chapters.title: A New Entry, Handwritten
chapters.summary: Back at the guild, Sable enters Thorn into the ledger not as an asset but as kin. Ferro plants a garden for the memory he lost; Maren maps a road home for future runaways. Beat: healing as deliberate practice.

chapters.title: Odile and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Wren—whose true name is Odile—speaks her first free sentence, naming the guild as home. Thorn, nameless but not alone, opens a fresh ledger page and writes nothing, leaving room for whatever comes. Beat: quiet hope; the story's themes resolved.
